key: Part, like a knotted tangle, while they cleanse thee, O Soma, righteous and unrighteous conduct.
s: After asking Soma to set the winds free like unbraided hair, the singer asks a second untying; Sāyaṇa, on 9.97.18, hears a plea that the singer, bound by sins, be untied from them like a knot, and given a straight path and strength.
src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 9.97.18, sa.wikisource ऋग्वेदः सूक्तं ९.९७, revision 402120 (2024)

evidence.words: पुनानः पूयमानस्त्वं ग्रथितं पापैर्बद्धं मां वि ष्य मुञ्च । पापेभ्यो विश्लेषय । कथमिव । ग्रन्थिं न यथा कश्चित् ग्रन्थिं विश्लेषयति । षो अन्तकर्मणि इत्यस्य लोटि रूपम् । किंच हे सोम त्वम् ऋजुम् अवक्रं गातुं मार्गं च वृजिनं बलं च मह्यं देहि ।
evidence.gloss: Being purified, loose me, who am tied, bound by sins: separate me from sins. How? As one unties a knot. (vi ṣya is the imperative of ṣo, to end.) And, Soma, give me a straight, uncrooked path and strength (vṛjina glossed as bala).

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, ref 9.97.18, at [819,18]). Sāyaṇa on 9.97.18 glosses grathitam as pāpair baddham mām, asks Soma to loose him from sins as one unties a knot, and asks for a straight path (ṛju gātu) and strength (vṛjina = bala); Wilson (vol. 5) translates the same way. The reading matches his words without drift. Plain sense: 9.97.17 asks Soma to set the Winds free like unbraided hair, 9.97.18 asks for a parting like a knotted tangle, so a second untying is faithful and names no commentator. src revision 402120 dated 2024-05-02 by the lock. entry-check ok.
